picks.headline: Guilt-free AI? What so-called “ethical AI” tools mean for musicians and producers
picks.excerpt: Amidst a mounting backlash, music AI companies are talking of ethics, responsibility and transparency – but what does it actually mean, and how can producers know which tools to trust?
picks.rationale: Freshest item in the pool and the most directly actionable: a buying/trust framework for deciding which AI music tools to put in a session.

picks.headline: AI ‘artists’ set to perform ‘live’ at first AI Music Awards in Los Angeles
picks.excerpt: The first AI Music Awards lands at The Mayan in LA on 13 November, with AI ‘artists’ including Xania Monet performing live. The human creators behind each act will be “directing the stage”, according to organisers SIQA.
picks.rationale: First-of-its-kind event that turns the AI-artist debate into a staged, dated reality — high novelty, nothing like it in the section history.

picks.headline: Why AI Workflows Need Music Understanding and Search
picks.excerpt: Conversational search and agentic music workflows only work when they are built on structured metadata that lets AI actually understand a catalogue. A look at what music understanding infrastructure means for creators and rights holders.
picks.rationale: The plumbing story behind every agentic music tool — metadata discipline is the concrete thing a catalogue owner can fix this week.

picks.headline: ReSing Voices Vol 2 from IK Multimedia
picks.excerpt: The latest expansion for IK Multimedia’s AI-powered vocal-modelling software has arrived, delivering a versatile set of new voice models aimed at modern music production tasks.
picks.rationale: Concrete shipped product for vocal production; distinct release from the Brazilian ReSing pack covered back in July.

picks.headline: DistroKid’s $2 billion valuation based on it being a pipeline for AI slop and copyright infringement, says Universal
picks.excerpt: Universal claims distributor DistroKid built its $2 billion valuation by acting as a pipeline for AI slop and copyright-infringing tracks. The suit puts distribution-side AI screening squarely on the agenda for every self-releasing artist.
picks.rationale: Major-label attack on the biggest indie distributor — changes the release-and-screening calculus for anyone self-distributing.
